---
title: "sample() on a single value draws from 1:value"
ref: LEN-11
categories: [Empty and NA]
impact: silencieux
extrait: 'length(sample(c(12)))'
reponse: '12'
attendu: "`1`, there is only one value to shuffle"
versions: "All"
source: "safer-r, The R Inferno"
---

::: {.piege}
```{r}
x <- c(3, 8, 12)
set.seed(42)
sample(x[x > 5])
set.seed(42)
sample(x[x > 10])
```
:::

## Why

`sample()` has two behaviours. Given a vector of several elements, it shuffles those elements. Given a single number `n`, it takes it as a size and draws from `1:n`.

As long as the filter keeps several values, all is well. The day it keeps only one, here 12, `sample()` returns a permutation of the integers from 1 to 12, which have nothing to do with the data.

## The remedy

Draw positions with `sample.int()`, then index the vector.

::: {.piege}
```{r}
selection <- x[x > 10]
set.seed(42)
selection[sample.int(length(selection))]
```
:::
